rows.name: Core compose services are up and healthy
rows.precondition: Docker daemon reachable; infra/docker-compose.yml present; no service stopped by hand
rows.action: docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d && docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml ps --format json
rows.expect: postgres, redis, mailpit and minio all report State=running and Health=healthy (or no healthcheck for mailpit)

rows.name: Postgres accepts connections on the exposed port
rows.precondition: compose postgres container running
rows.action: sh scripts/wait-for-postgres.sh
rows.expect: exit code 0 within 60s (pg_isready or TCP fallback succeeds)

rows.name: Every migration file is applied to the dev database
rows.precondition: Postgres reachable; apps/api/migrations/*.sql contains the migration set
rows.action: docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d $POSTGRES_DB -tAc "select count(*) from __app_migrations"
rows.expect: applied migration count equals the number of apps/api/migrations/*.sql files, is greater than 0, and the __app_migrations table exists

rows.name: Redis answers PING
rows.precondition: compose redis container running
rows.action: docker compose exec -T redis redis-cli PING
rows.expect: stdout contains PONG

rows.name: MinIO is live and the uploads bucket exists
rows.precondition: compose minio + minio-init services ran; S3_BUCKET set
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$S3_PORT/minio/health/live, then `docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh minio-init -c "mc alias set local http://minio:9000 ... && mc ls local/$S3_BUCKET"` plus the same `mc ls` against a definitely-missing bucket
rows.expect: health endpoint returns 200; mc lists the configured bucket successfully and fails for the unknown bucket (the S3 HTTP API answers 403 for both, so it cannot prove existence on its own)

rows.name: Mailpit HTTP API answers and exposes the message list
rows.precondition: compose mailpit container running; MAILPIT_HTTP_PORT reachable
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$MAILPIT_HTTP_PORT/api/v1/messages
rows.expect: HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing a numeric `total` and a `messages` array

rows.name: Optional replication pair: replica is in recovery mode
rows.precondition: compose `topology` profile running (topology-primary + topology-replica containers up); skipped otherwise
rows.action: docker compose exec -T topology-replica psql -U postgres -tAc "select pg_is_in_recovery()"
rows.expect: stdout is `t` for the replica and `f` for the primary; row is reported as skipped (not failed) when the profile is not running

rows.name: Liveness probe answers on the API port
rows.precondition: API started from dist with the dev .env; DB reachable
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$API_PORT/api/v1/health
rows.expect: HTTP 200, envelope data.status == "ok" and data.warnings is an array

rows.name: Readiness probe confirms dependency health
rows.precondition: API started; Postgres reachable
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$API_PORT/api/v1/health/ready
rows.expect: HTTP 200 and data.status == "ready"

rows.name: OpenAPI UI and raw document are served
rows.precondition: API started with API_DOCS_ENABLED=true and APP_ENV!=production
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$API_PORT/api/docs and GET http://localhost:$API_PORT/api/docs-json
rows.expect: docs UI returns 200 with HTML; docs-json returns 200 with an `openapi` version string and at least 50 documented paths

rows.name: Registration is completed by the emailed verification link
rows.precondition: API + worker running; Mailpit reachable; registration_enabled=true
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/register with a unique email, then read the message from Mailpit GET /api/v1/messages + GET /api/v1/message/{ID}, extract ?token= from the verify-email link, POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email, then POST /api/v1/auth/login
rows.expect: register 201 with data.success=true; a verify-email message for that recipient arrives in Mailpit within 60s; verify-email 201 success=true; login 201 with accessToken+refreshToken and a single USER role; login before verification is rejected

rows.name: me, refresh and logout rotate the session correctly
rows.precondition: Seeded admin exists and is ACTIVE
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/login; GET /api/v1/auth/me; POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the returned refreshToken; POST /api/v1/auth/logout with the refreshed access token; GET /api/v1/auth/me again
rows.expect: login 201; me 200 with user.email and a non-empty permissions array; refresh 201 issuing a new accessToken different from the previous one; logout 201 success=true; the post-logout me request returns 401 with error.code AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED (logout revokes the session, and the guard reports that specific reason)

rows.name: Wrong password is rejected with 401
rows.precondition: API reachable
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/login with a valid email and a wrong password
rows.expect: HTTP 401 and error.code == "AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS"; no accessToken in the body

rows.name: Protected routes reject anonymous callers
rows.precondition: API reachable
rows.action: GET /api/v1/users/me and GET /api/v1/admin/users with no Authorization header
rows.expect: both return HTTP 401 with error.code == "AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED"

rows.name: A USER-only account is forbidden on admin routes
rows.precondition: A verified account holding only the USER platform role (created by the register row)
rows.action: GET /api/v1/admin/users and GET /api/v1/admin/settings with the USER access token
rows.expect: both return HTTP 403 with error.code == "AUTH_FORBIDDEN"; the same token still succeeds (200) on GET /api/v1/activities

rows.name: Two organizations cannot read each other's users
rows.precondition: Super admin session; platform ADMIN role id from GET /api/v1/admin/roles; seeded admin and seeded user own distinct organizations
rows.action: POST /api/v1/admin/users twice to create org-admin-a (in org A) and org-admin-b (in org B); log in as each and complete the forced password change; then as org-admin-a GET /api/v1/admin/users and GET /api/v1/admin/users/{orgAdminBId}
rows.expect: the org A user list never contains org-admin-b's email; reading org-admin-b's user id directly returns 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN

rows.name: TOTP enrolment gates the next login
rows.precondition: Verified account with a session; server clock within one TOTP window of the harness
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup; POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm with a wrong code then with a valid TOTP code derived from data.secret; POST /api/v1/auth/login; POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify-challenge with a wrong code, a valid code and then the same valid code again; POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/disable
rows.expect: setup 201 returns secret+otpauthUrl; wrong confirm 401 MFA_INVALID_CODE; valid confirm 201 returns 8 recovery codes and status.enabled becomes true; login 201 returns mfaRequired=true with mfaToken and no accessToken; wrong challenge 401 MFA_INVALID_CODE; valid challenge 201 issues tokens; replaying the same challenge 401 MFA_CHALLENGE_INVALID; disable 201 and status.enabled returns to false

rows.name: maintenance_mode blocks traffic with 503 and is reversible
rows.precondition: Super admin session; settings seeded with maintenance_mode.enabled=false
rows.action: PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings/maintenance_mode {"value":{"enabled":true}}; GET /api/v1/users/me; GET /api/v1/health; PATCH the same key back to {"enabled":false,"message":null}; GET /api/v1/users/me
rows.expect: toggle 200; while enabled /api/v1/users/me returns 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE while /api/v1/health still returns 200 (health is exempt); after the revert /api/v1/users/me returns 200 again

rows.name: registration_enabled=false closes self-signup
rows.precondition: Super admin session; settings seeded with registration_enabled.enabled=true
rows.action: PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings/registration_enabled {"value":{"enabled":false}}; POST /api/v1/auth/register with a fresh email; PATCH back to {"enabled":true}
rows.expect: while disabled the register call returns 403 with error.code == "SETTINGS_REGISTRATION_DISABLED" and no user is created; afterwards register returns 201 for the same email

rows.name: File upload, listing, signed download and delete
rows.precondition: Super admin session; object storage reachable
rows.action: POST /api/v1/files (multipart field `file`) with a text fixture; GET /api/v1/files?search=...; GET /api/v1/files/{id}/url; GET the returned url with the session; GET /api/v1/files/{id}/download?token=... with no session; DELETE /api/v1/files/{id}; GET /api/v1/files?search=... again
rows.expect: upload 201 with id/sizeBytes/checksum; the list returns the new file; /url returns a signed url plus expiresInSeconds; fetching that url with the session returns 200 with byte-identical content; the same url without a session returns 401 (the token is an extra factor, not a replacement for auth); delete 200 success=true; the final list no longer contains the file

rows.name: Upload policy rejects disallowed extensions
rows.precondition: Super admin session
rows.action: POST /api/v1/files with a .exe attachment
rows.expect: HTTP 400 with error.message mentioning the unsupported extension; no file row is created

rows.name: A templated mail is queued, rendered and delivered to SMTP
rows.precondition: Super admin session; worker running (outbox + job processors); Mailpit reachable
rows.action: POST /api/v1/admin/mail/send {templateKey:"auth.welcome",to,variables:{displayName,adminUrl}}; poll GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}; GET http://localhost:$MAILPIT_HTTP_PORT/api/v1/messages; GET /api/v1/admin/mail/deliveries
rows.expect: send 201 returns a jobId with status PENDING; the job reaches COMPLETED; a message addressed to the recipient with subject containing "Welcome" appears in Mailpit; the delivery audit row reports status SENT

rows.name: Reserved templates and missing variables are refused
rows.precondition: Super admin session; template catalogue loaded
rows.action: GET /api/v1/admin/mail/templates; POST /api/v1/admin/mail/send for auth.reset-password; POST /api/v1/admin/mail/send for auth.welcome without the adminUrl variable
rows.expect: the catalogue marks auth.reset-password and auth.verify-email as sendable=false and auth.welcome as sendable=true; the reserved template returns 400; the missing variable returns 400 mentioning the variable name

rows.name: An enqueued job is executed by the worker to COMPLETED
rows.precondition: Worker running with the job scheduler; super admin session with jobs.read
rows.action: POST /api/v1/admin/mail/send to obtain a jobId; poll GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId} until terminal; GET /api/v1/admin/jobs?type=mail.send
rows.expect: the job is observable via GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{id} with type mail.send, reaches COMPLETED, attempts >= 1, completedAt set and errorMessage null; the jobs list includes it

rows.name: An admin notification lands in the target user's inbox
rows.precondition: Super admin session; seeded user id from login; seeded user session
rows.action: POST /api/v1/admin/notifications {audience:"USER",userId:<a user from another organization>} (must be refused); POST /api/v1/admin/notifications {audience:"ALL",type,title,body}; GET /api/v1/notifications with the sender token; GET /api/v1/notifications with the other-organization user token; GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count
rows.expect: targeting a user outside the actor organization returns 400; the organization-wide send returns 201 with status COMPLETED and recipientCount >= 1; the sender inbox contains the new title and type; the other organization's inbox does not receive it; unread-count is at least 1

rows.name: A users export is produced by the worker and downloadable
rows.precondition: Super admin session with an active organization; worker running the export processor
rows.action: POST /api/v1/exports {type:"users"}; poll GET /api/v1/exports/{id} until terminal; GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/url then GET that url with the session
rows.expect: create 201 returns status PENDING; the export reaches COMPLETED with a fileId within 180s; the signed url returns 200 with a CSV whose header is email,displayName,avatarUrl and which contains the seeded admin email

rows.name: A CSV import is previewed and committed through /imports
rows.precondition: Super admin session; upload privilege
rows.action: POST /api/v1/files with a users CSV (header email,displayName,avatarUrl) containing one new address; POST /api/v1/imports {type:"users",fileId}; POST /api/v1/imports/{id}/confirm; GET /api/v1/admin/users?search=<new address>
rows.expect: create 201; confirm returns a terminal status COMPLETED with an empty error list; the imported address becomes visible in the admin user list

rows.name: Privileged actions leave activity and audit trails
rows.precondition: Super admin session with an organization; at least one prior write action in this run
rows.action: GET /api/v1/activities and GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs with the super admin token; then perform an admin notification send and re-read both
rows.expect: activities returns 200 with a numeric total and rows carrying entityType/entityId; audit logs return 200 with total greater than zero; the audit total grows after the notification send

rows.name: Invalid payloads are rejected with 400 and field details
rows.precondition: API reachable
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/login with {"email":"not-an-email"} and an unknown body field
rows.expect: HTTP 400 with error.code == "VALIDATION_FAILED" and error.details being a non-empty array of messages (the platform standardises payload validation on 400; there is no 422 contract in the OpenAPI document)

rows.name: Unknown routes return 404 without leaking internals
rows.precondition: API reachable
rows.action: GET /api/v1/this-route-does-not-exist
rows.expect: HTTP 404, error.message states the route cannot be served, and the response contains no stack trace

rows.name: Duplicate registration is a 409 conflict
rows.precondition: An account exists for the address (created by the register row)
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/register twice with the same email
rows.expect: the second call returns HTTP 409 with error.code == "USER_EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS" and no new user row is created

rows.name: The login route enforces its rate limit
rows.precondition: Login limit is 5 per 60s. The row clears the rate-limit counters (and waits out a block if Redis is not backing the limiter) before measuring and after finishing, so it neither inherits nor leaves a blocked login window
rows.action: POST /api/v1/auth/login six times in a row with a nonexistent account; then clear the counters again and probe the route once
rows.expect: attempts 1-5 return 401 (never 429) and attempt 6 returns 429 with error.message containing "Too Many Requests"; the cleanup probe then answers 401, proving the window is usable again for the rows that follow

rows.name: Public home page renders the landing content
rows.precondition: web built and started on WEB_PORT
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$WEB_PORT/ and GET http://localhost:$WEB_PORT/en
rows.expect: root redirects to the default locale (/en) with 3xx; /en returns 200 HTML containing the Super Template title and the landing headline

rows.name: The Vietnamese locale is served
rows.precondition: web running
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$WEB_PORT/vi
rows.expect: HTTP 200 HTML from the same landing component (locale prefix is always present, so /vi is a distinct route that renders)

rows.name: Web does not host its own login page; admin owns authentication
rows.precondition: web running
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$WEB_PORT/login and GET http://localhost:$WEB_PORT/en/login
rows.expect: the request is redirected to /en/login and then answered with 404 (the public app has no login route by design); the landing page links to the admin app as the only sign-in surface

rows.name: Public web has no authenticated area to redirect from
rows.precondition: web running
rows.action: not automated: the web app only serves /, /vi, /en and /{locale}/verify-email plus /api/auth/* route handlers; there is no protected route
rows.expect: not applicable - the protected-route redirect requirement is covered by admin-protected-route-redirects; recorded here so the coverage gap is explicit rather than silently dropped

rows.name: Playwright end-to-end suite passes against the running stack
rows.precondition: web, admin and api started by this harness; PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_WEBSERVER=1 so Playwright reuses them; database migrated and seeded
rows.action: PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_WEBSERVER=1 pnpm --filter web test:e2e
rows.expect: playwright test exits 0 with every spec passing (landing, admin smoke and admin resource routes)

rows.name: Admin login page renders server-side
rows.precondition: admin built and started on ADMIN_PORT
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$ADMIN_PORT/en/login
rows.expect: HTTP 200 returning the admin app HTML shell (title "Super Admin"). The login form itself is client-rendered after hydration, so its copy is asserted by the browser suite in web-e2e-playwright-suite rather than by this HTTP probe

rows.name: Anonymous access to an admin page redirects to login
rows.precondition: admin running; no session cookie sent
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$ADMIN_PORT/en/users and GET http://localhost:$ADMIN_PORT/users without cookies
rows.expect: both answer with an HTTP redirect whose Location points at the locale-prefixed login route, and no admin markup is returned

rows.name: A real refresh-token cookie opens the admin shell
rows.precondition: A real super admin session obtained from the API login endpoint
rows.action: GET http://localhost:$ADMIN_PORT/en with Cookie st_admin_refresh_token=<refresh token from the API login>
rows.expect: HTTP 200 HTML (the edge proxy admits the request once the refresh cookie is present) and the same request without the cookie redirects to login. Authenticated dashboard content is asserted by the Playwright admin smoke spec in web-e2e-playwright-suite

rows.name: Main admin pages render behind the session gate
rows.precondition: admin running; refresh-token cookie present
rows.action: GET /en/users, /en/roles, /en/audit-logs, /en/settings, /en/jobs, /en/mail with the cookie
rows.expect: every route returns HTTP 200 with the admin HTML shell and none returns 5xx or a login redirect (page content hydrates client-side, so data rendering is covered by the browser suite)

rows.name: The seeded super admin can read every admin API surface
rows.precondition: Seeded SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL/SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD; API running
rows.action: GET /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/admin/roles, /api/v1/admin/audit-logs, /api/v1/admin/settings, /api/v1/admin/jobs with the super admin token
rows.expect: each endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an envelope (data present, no error object)

rows.name: Flutter format check, analyzer and widget tests pass
rows.precondition: Flutter SDK on PATH (the harness prepends a locally installed SDK when it is not on PATH)
rows.action: pnpm run mobile:check (turbo -> dart format --set-exit-if-changed, flutter analyze, flutter test)
rows.expect: exit code 0 with no unformatted file, no analyzer error and all widget tests passing

rows.name: Release APK builds from the mobile app
rows.precondition: Flutter SDK plus Android SDK/JDK 17 available
rows.action: pnpm run mobile:build (flutter build apk --release --dart-define-from-file=env/prod.json)
rows.expect: exit code 0 and apps/mobile/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk exists and is non-empty

rows.name: On-device / emulator E2E for the mobile app
rows.precondition: A booted emulator or attached device with adb access
rows.action: not automated: no emulator or physical device is available in this environment, so integration_test cannot be driven
rows.expect: out of scope for this run - the automated proxy is app-mobile-check plus app-mobile-build-apk (compile, lint, widget tests, installable artifact); device E2E stays a manual/release-pipeline step

rows.name: Architecture and source policy checks pass
rows.precondition: Repository installed with node_modules present
rows.action: pnpm run lint:policy
rows.expect: exit code 0 (source policy, web boundaries, package cycles, cross-feature FKs, error codes, domain purity, turbo boundaries)

rows.name: Whole workspace typechecks
rows.precondition: node_modules installed
rows.action: pnpm exec turbo run typecheck
rows.expect: exit code 0

rows.name: Whole workspace unit tests pass
rows.precondition: node_modules installed
rows.action: pnpm exec turbo run test
rows.expect: exit code 0

rows.name: Schema and migration state are in sync
rows.precondition: Postgres reachable
rows.action: pnpm run schema:check
rows.expect: exit code 0

rows.name: Generated contracts and artefacts show no drift
rows.precondition: node_modules installed
rows.action: pnpm run generate:check
rows.expect: exit code 0 (no regeneration diff)

rows.name: The API end-to-end suite passes
rows.precondition: Postgres reachable; DATABASE_URL_TEST and DATABASE_URL_TEST_ADMIN point at the test database
rows.action: pnpm --filter api test:e2e
rows.expect: exit code 0 with every e2e spec passing (the suite resets and seeds its own test database)

rows.name: Formatting gate passes
rows.precondition: node_modules installed
rows.action: pnpm run format:check
rows.expect: exit code 0 (prettier reports no unformatted file under packages/**, apps/api, apps/admin, apps/web)
